subject: wizardBookshelf
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: wizard's bookshelf with tomes, scrolls, orbs and candles.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a wizard's bookshelf scene with tomes, scrolls, orbs, and candles in a high-fantasy anime style, using the agentic-3js-builder SDK with toon and glow kits, and building parts via extrude, lathe, sweep, and card primitives without joints.

Now I'm figuring out the shelf unit dimensions, a wooden frame with sides, five shelves, a back panel, and crown finial, plus books rendered as colored boxes with gold stripe trim and SVG textures for spines and scroll parchment, using the paint API for wood grain effects.

For props like orbs on lathed pedestals, candles with glowing flames, and horizontal scroll cylinders with parchment caps, I'm deciding to skip joints entirely since static models can omit them, letting parts default to root model space, keeping things simple while centering the shelf along x and facing it in the +Z direction.

I'm defining the shelf's overall dimensions—width, height, depth—with side panels, a base plinth, and four horizontal shelves at specific heights with board thickness, leaving compartment gaps sized for books up to 0.42 tall. I'm writing a helper function to place boxes with position, size, color, and optional texture, then using it to scatter randomized books along each shelf with varying widths, heights, and colors drawn from a palette.

Now I'm adding details like gold decorative bands on spines, occasional title-labeled spine textures, some books lying flat on top of stacks, and scrolls made from cylinders with ribbon accents placed in a few compartments, orienting the cylinder geometry to lie horizontally along the shelf.

Next I'm working out glowing crystal orbs on pedestals built from lathe-generated profiles, plus candles made from cream-colored cylinders topped with small glowing flame spheres and brass lathe holders, finishing with a decorative finial crest at the very top of the bookcase.

For decoration, I'm generating SVG spine labels with gold rectangles and dark painted text paths for the book textures, planning a few label variants, and importing the glow kit to apply glowing effects to the orbs and candle flames.

I'm also planning to use wood grain paint for the shelves and a plain painted back panel, then sketching out the module structure with the builder, rng, paint, grain, mottle, and svg utilities, plus the glow kit import, defining the part/lathe/root hierarchy and part options like position, direction, and texture.

Now I'm sketching the actual dimensions: side panels, a thin back panel, four shelf boards plus a top board, and a plinth base, working out their positions and resolving a conflict between the bottom shelf and plinth height.

Then I'm figuring out shelf y-positions and compartment heights so books fit without clipping into the shelf above, and planning a loop that fills each compartment with books of randomized widths until the available space runs out.

Spine labels use textures applied across the whole box since the box is thin enough that the texture shows on the front face too, so color choice doesn't matter much since the drawn texture includes its own background fill. For counts, roughly 4 compartments times 20 books times 3 parts each gives about 240 parts total, which is manageable. I'm also considering lying/stacked books as a separate category.

I'm placing a stack of 2-3 flat books at the end of a compartment using thin boxes, plus adding lying scrolls as cylinders oriented horizontally in gap regions so they don't overlap the standing books -- having some compartments' books stop short of the full width to leave room for scrolls, candles, and orbs to fill the remaining space.

Planning out each compartment: assigning different book-fill widths per shelf, adding a candle holder near one gap, and placing a glowing orb on a small pedestal in another. For the top area, I'm adding a crown finial and two pedestal-mounted orbs symmetrically placed near the edges of the top shelf.

Now detailing the finishing touches: candle geometry with a brass holder, wax cylinder, and glowing flame; scroll props as parchment-colored cylinders wrapped with a thin ribbon box; and the orb's glowing sphere sitting atop its pedestal. Finishing with the finial spire at the very top of the shelf.

Adding crown rim and trim, plus wood grain texture...

Writing the box helper function...

Drawing a book spine texture with worn edges and decorative lines...

Now I'm thinking through runes design with opaque indigo background and gold markings, then writing the loop logic to populate each shelf with randomly sized books, skipping gaps occasionally and varying width, height, and depth for variety.

I realize passing an undefined texture property could break the part-checking logic, so I should only include the texture key conditionally when it's actually defined, rather than always passing it as undefined.

Adding scroll details...

Still placing candles and flames... Then I'm adding the glowing orb in compartment 2 on a lathe pedestal, plus the top pedestal orbs in red with glow, and a crown finial lathe shape at the very top.

Now I'm checking the shelf spacing - with shelves at 0.12, 0.62, 1.12, 1.62, 2.08, that gives four compartments, but the last one is only 0.46 tall instead of 0.5, so I need to verify my tallest books (up to 0.44 height) don't collide with the top board, since the board's underside sits at 2.0625 and my books could reach 2.0775 - a slight intrusion I need to fix.

I'm capping book heights at 0.4 max for safety, which keeps the tallest books comfortably under each shelf board with margin to spare, and now I'm working out exactly where to place objects in each compartment - books clustered toward one side, scrolls and candles filling the remaining space, varying positions across the four compartments so the shelf doesn't look repetitive.

For compartment 2 I'm placing the orb alongside a short stack of lying books around x 0.24-0.4, sizing the lying book box roughly 0.2 wide and 0.24 deep to fit beside the orb without collision.

Defining the lathe profile for the orb pedestal, computing orb center position, and confirming the glow function works with Part objects. Now finalizing the code at roughly 200 lines with the meta export included.
